method_card.title: Proportion with Powers & Roots
method_card.content:
Higher-tier proportion uses powers and roots. Read the statement, then build an equation with a constant k.

Direct: y ∝ x² gives y = kx²; y ∝ x³ gives y = kx³; y ∝ √x gives y = k√x.

Inverse: y ∝ 1/x² gives y = k/x².

Find k from the pair you are given, write the full equation, then substitute the new value. Always apply the power or root to x before multiplying by k.
method_card.example:
y ∝ x². When x = 3, y = 45. Find y when x = 4.

y = kx² → 45 = k(9) → k = 5.

y = 5(4²) = 5(16) = 80.

steps: Find n: if multiplying x by a factor f multiplies y by g, then fⁿ = g. Match the power.
Chains: combine two statements. If P ∝ 1/V and V ∝ T, then P ∝ 1/T.
Roots count as powers: √x is x to the power a half.
